topic: DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite sub-5GB rebuild running on a 6GB GPU
title: DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite on a 6GB GPU: 65 tok/s
description: Working description; the package stage overwrites this. A rebuilt sub-5GB GGUF fits DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite entirely in 6GB of VRAM.

narration_full: Your old GPU isn't too small for DeepSeek. The rebuilt file: four point eight three gigabytes of weights. One author ran every layer on a six-gigabyte laptop card. The speed: sixty-five to seventy-six tokens a second. The belief it breaks: big models need big cards. DeepSeek Coder V two Lite does store sixteen billion parameters. Two point four billion wake per word. Mixture of experts: many specialists, few called per word. Memory pays them all. The rebuild rounds weights down and cuts the ten least-called experts. The myth survives: nobody re-measured the pruned file's accuracy, and that speed is one self-reported run. Your card wasn't too small; the file was too big.

notes_for_review: Speed figure is one author's self-reported run on an RTX 4050 6GB laptop GPU; pruned container accuracy was never re-measured. Both are hedged in narration.
